title: 1994 AHSME Problem 26
statement: A regular polygon of \(m\) sides is exactly enclosed (no overlaps, no gaps) by \(m\) regular polygons of \(n\) sides each. (Shown here for \(m=4,\) \(n=8.\)) If \(m=10,\) what is the value of \(n?\)

solutions.text: At a vertex of the inner polygon, its interior angle and two angles from the surrounding polygons total \(360^\circ.\) Thus \[ \begin{gathered} 180^\circ\left(1-\frac2m\right) \\ {}+2\cdot180^\circ\left(1-\frac2n\right)\\ {}=360^\circ. \end{gathered} \] This simplifies to \(\frac{1}{m}+\frac{2}{n}=\frac{1}{2}.\) With \(m=10,\) we get \(\frac{2}{n}=\frac{2}{5},\) so \(n=5.\) Thus the correct answer is A.
hints: At each vertex of the inner polygon, one \(m\)-gon angle and two \(n\)-gon angles fill \(360^\circ\)
